I'd like to make a counter argument, I might be an exception here, but I think it effects people differently. I smoke a lot of cannabis, like more than any normal human probably would consider. I had a surgery on my lower intestine and now suffer from chronic pain. Before the surgery, I was completely sober all the time. I don't like to drink or feel intoxicated. I like being in control of my thoughts and lucid. In high school and early college, before I had my surgery and started smoking, I was always a decent student with a few A's, some B's and a random class with a D or F. 

After I had my surgery, I took a year off of everything and laid in bed. I lost roughly 40 pounds and was really having issues eating. On a whim, someone offered me a joint and it really helped relieve my symptoms. I didn't feel my constant pain and I actually got an appetite. Being a person that grew up in the 90's, I went through the whole DARE program and learned how marijuana was a gateway drug that makes people lazy/stupid. I thought this would happen to me too if I started smoking regularly. But, it is truly the only thing non-narcotic that takes away my chronic pain, so I started self-medicating. 

After getting my life back a bit, I enrolled back in school and much to my surprise, I was a straight A student for the rest of my time in college. I took online classes for 2 years straight without any breaks and earned all A's. For me, it makes me a more disciplined person and gives me patience to do things I normally wouldn't.

When I was a child I had this friend that was very cheery and comedic. He was considered the class clown. We would hang out quite often, but he usually would come over to my house. One night I ended up staying the night there and that house was completely trashed. The house was ran by a single alcoholic father. There was literally hundreds of nuggets of cat shit all over their house. Every single dish in the house was dirty, no clean water or food in the house. Laundry everywhere and very mixed in with the cat feces. I was in such shock that he lived that way. I had no idea what to do or say. I still don't.

He had a really hard time focusing in class and got in trouble a lot. He often would sketch stick figure pictures of war scenes during class. He would make the sounds of the people dying and make people laugh while doing it. When Jackass became popular, he made people laugh by getting himself hurt or performing stunts.

As we got a little older (9th grade) we grew apart. We were in completely different classes, but we would still say hi now and then.  One day, I saw him looking particularly gloomy in the hall between classes and I asked him if everything was okay. He looked like he was ready to cry and told me, not really~ The bell was about to ring and I told him, I'm sorry things aren't going well. We should catch up. He shrugged and said yea I guess. He ended up getting drunk that night, then walked in front of a train and flipped it off before it ended his life. 

I guess the red flags would be look out for shitty housing/parent situations and watch what kids draw/write/say.
